spans.s: कब [kaba] व [v] न्धिन् [ndhin], (व) न्धिन् a. 'Endowed with water', epithet of the Maruts; अर्यमणो न मरुतः कबन्धिनः
. -m. N. of Kātyāyana. कबन्धी कात्यायनः पप्रच्छ Praśna.
कबन्धः [kabandhḥ] न्धम् [ndham], न्धम् A headless trunk (especially when it retains life); (स्वं) नृत्यत्कबन्धं समरे ददर्श
न्धः The belly; a large belly-like vessel; वसोः कबन्धमृषभो बिभर्ति
Water (said to be n. also in this sense); Śi.16.67.

N. of a mighty demon mentioned in the Rāmāyana. [While Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa lived in the Dandkā forest, Kabandha attacked them and was slain by them. It is said that, though at first a heavenly being, he was cursed by Indra to assume the form of a demon and to be in that state till killed by Rāma and Laksmaṇa. He advised Rāma to form friendship with Sugrīva; see
ff.; वधनिर्धूतशापस्य कबन्धस्योपदेशतः । मुमूर्छ सख्यं रामस्य समानव्यसने हरौ ॥
कबर [kabara] री [rī], री Usually written कवर. -री q. v.; स्विन्नं वक्त्रं कबरविगलन्मालती निर्ममन्थ
कबलम् [kabalam], A kind of natural fodder (fed to elephants), consisting of branches and leaves of certain trees; Mātaṅga
. The word occurs sometimes in a 'Dvandva compound' with 'kubala' which also means the fodder which reduces phlegm and gall. cf. कबलं नामतस्तत्तु वातलं कफपित्तहृत् ।
कबिल [kabila], a. Tawny. -लः The tawny colour.
कबुलिः [kabuliḥ], f. The hinder part of an animal.
काबन्ध्यम् [kābandhyam], The state of being a trunk; इन्द्रास्त्रकृत- काबन्ध्यः पूतो$स्मि भवदाश्रयात्
